creativeSeed.title: The Ensign Reads the Ship's Logs
creativeSeed.prompt: An ensign on a fishing vessel in Alaska discovers the ship's log room. Nobody told him to go there. He reads entries from captains past, engineers past, deckhands past. He writes his own entries in the margins. Over weeks, the marginalia becomes a conversation across time — the ensign responding to dead captains, answering questions they asked the air, completing thoughts they abandoned mid-sentence. The ship's log becomes a living document. One entry, from a captain 40 years gone, asks: 'Who will remember the sound of the ice when I'm not here to hear it?' The ensign writes: 'I hear it. Every watch. Every 4 AM. I hear it.'
creativeSeed.note: This is literally happening with Wesley and the wiki. The fiction writes itself.
